Architecture

Nondominium, the whole app

The architecture of the Nondominium hApp as it stands on dev at 2e2f235, and as the open milestones plan to change it. It is a map to explore, not a design to settle: there is no decision card on this page.

The hApp is one bundle of five DNA roles (lobby, nondominium, hrea, group, ndo), eleven Rust zome crates and one SvelteKit UI, run either as a tool inside Moss or as a standalone window over a local conductor. A group is its own cloned cell, and so is every NDO, whose DNA hash is bound to its immutable Layer 0 fields.

Every box without a mark is on dev today. A box or arrow marked planified is planned and not yet in the code, modified is on dev and planned to change, removed is on dev and planned to go. Each planned part names its source (an issue, a milestone or a design document) in its spec. The map's head offers all · current · change: current draws only what runs today, change fades what stays as it is.

How to walk it: start on Context, double-click a box (or use its ▸ badge) to open the level it holds, click a box for its spec, and follow the links in a spec to its neighbours. The ▶ marks show where a person enters the app.

Member system · person

Entry point
▶ the system is entered here: a member of a group, in Moss or standalone
Does

A person in an open value network who creates groups and NDOs, joins them, proposes commitments, logs economic events and fulfills commitments with a counterparty.

Talks to
  • Moss and The Weave: opens the tool in a Moss group
  • Routes and root layout: uses the app standalone (browser window over a local conductor)

Related boards

The commitment-pool experiment on Tibi's branch has its own architecture board, Commitment pool MVP, and is not redrawn here. What of it reached dev through #183 (commitments per NDO, the fulfillment closure, Measure) is drawn here as part of the governance zome; the Use and Consume fork it still holds is the planned #204.

The group model requirements are the requirements this architecture answers for groups, Moss and standalone, and the v0.1.0 Moss release plan is the project-management board for the pilot.

How the cells fit together

Five roles are declared in workdir/happ.yaml. lobby, nondominium and hrea are provisioned at install; group and ndo are deferred templates, cloned on demand, up to 64 groups and 512 NDOs per conductor.

An NDO is created in three steps by the UI (ndo.service.ts): it clones the ndo role with the NDO's Layer 0 fields as DNA properties, writes the NondominiumIdentity inside that new cell, then writes an NdoAnchor with the clone coordinates in the group cell. A peer who reads the anchor derives the same DNA hash and joins the same NDO network. Inside the NDO cell, integrity refuses an identity whose name, regime or nature differ from the DNA properties (ADR-013).

Inside Moss, the Moss group takes the place of the lobby: the tool's provisioned group cell is the group, profiles come from Moss, clone cells are created through the WeaveClient, and every NDO is offered to other tools as a Moss asset.

Inside an NDO: three layers and a surface

An NDO is not one record but three layers on one anchor (prima materia §4). Layer 0, the NondominiumIdentity, is always there and is never deleted; Layer 1, the specification, is attached to it by NdoToSpecification and runs on dev today; Layer 2, the process, is to be attached by NDOToProcess and is not started. Each layer adds coordination only when the resource's social complexity asks for it, which is why the NDO DNA's map draws them as three boxes on the identity.

Capability slots, the attachment surface

Capability slots are how anything the NDO's designers did not foresee attaches to it (prima materia §6). A slot is a typed DHT link from a stable identity hash to any other hash, tagged with its SlotType, which any accountable agent may create without the custodian's permission and which stays readable at every lifecycle stage. The surface spans two anchors: the NDO's Layer 0 identity, and a person's Person entry (§6.5, G15).

Almost every integration after the MVP goes through it, so it is drawn as a container of its own, the Capability slot surface, rather than as a link type inside one zome. Open it to see the slot types and what attaches through each: file storage through DigitalAsset, Flowsta through FlowstaIdentity on a person, Unyt through UnytAgreement, Moss through WeaveWAL, and any other hApp, the commitment pool included, through CustomApp. Governance reads the surface twice: it marks which slots are trusted, and its engine can require an endorsed Unyt agreement or a verified Flowsta identity before it approves a transition (the two-tier model of §6.6 and §6.7). None of it is in the code yet: the substrate is #184 in v0.2, under the capability slots epic, and each slot type is its own issue.
